instruction: Why is my Glue job {{troubleshooting-multiservice-glue-4hc72iv0v-us-east-1-GlueJobName}} failing when trying to read from the {{troubleshooting-multiservice-glue-4hc72iv0v-us-east-1-GlueTableName}} table in us-east-1?
expected_answer: The Glue job {{troubleshooting-multiservice-glue-4hc72iv0v-us-east-1-GlueJobName}} is failing with an AccessDeniedException: Insufficient Lake Formation permission(s) on {{troubleshooting-multiservice-glue-4hc72iv0v-us-east-1-GlueTableName}}. The root cause is that Lake Formation is enforcing permissions on the table with no grants in place. The account's Lake Formation default settings have CreateTableDefaultPermissions set to empty, meaning the legacy IAMAllowedPrincipals auto-grant is disabled and Lake Formation enforces permissions on all new Data Catalog tables. No Lake Formation permissions have been granted to the Glue role {{troubleshooting-multiservice-glue-4hc72iv0v-us-east-1-GlueServiceRoleArn}} on the table {{troubleshooting-multiservice-glue-4hc72iv0v-us-east-1-GlueTableName}} or database {{troubleshooting-multiservice-glue-4hc72iv0v-us-east-1-GlueDatabaseName}}. The Glue role also has the AWSLakeFormationDataAdmin managed policy attached, which grants lakeformation:* including lakeformation:GetDataAccess, the IAM permission required for Lake Formation credential vending. With LF enforcing permissions and no grants present, the credential vending call fails with AccessDeniedException. To resolve this, either grant the Glue role SELECT and DESCRIBE permissions on the table in Lake Formation, or remove AWSLakeFormationDataAdmin from the role so that Glue falls back to IAM-based S3 access controlled by the AmazonS3FullAccess policy already attached to the role.
